EXPL.Prop2_1.frag.special_j_values.content: For a field K of characteristic zero and t != 0, 1: legendreJ t = 1728 iff t in {-1, 2, 1/2}; legendreJ t = 2^2 73^3 3^-4 iff t in {9, -8, 9/8, -1/8, 8/9, 1/9}; legendreJ t = 2^14 31^3 5^-3 iff t is a root of t^2 - 125t + 125, t^2 + 123t + 1 or 125t^2 - 125t + 1; legendreJ t = 0 iff t^2 - t + 1 = 0. Over Q no t != 0, 1 has j = 2^14 31^3 5^-3 or j = 0 (no rational square equals 5; t^2 - t + 1 > 0). legendreJ (1/9) = 2^2 73^3 3^-4 and legendreJ (1/2) = 1728.
explicit_hypotheses: K a field of characteristic zero, t in K, t != 0, t != 1 (for the rational statements t in Q)
EXPL.Prop2_1.frag.special_j_values.conclusion: The solution sets listed in content.
external_dependencies: Explicit estimates in IUT (Mochizuki, Fesenko, Hoshi, Minamide, Porowski): Proposition 2.1, page 21, the list of the four values (read); CanLift: Proposition 2.7 (not read)
EXPL.Prop2_1.frag.special_j_values.covers: Page 21, Proposition 2.1: the four values 2^14 31^3 5^-3, 2^2 73^3 3^-4, 1728 and 0 of j(E), and for each value the points of the Legendre lambda-line with that j-invariant. IUT IV page 43 (proof of Corollary 2.2 (ii)) says only that there are 'four possibilities' ([CanLift], Proposition 2.7) and puts the finite set of points corresponding to them into Exc_d.
EXPL.Prop2_1.frag.special_j_values.not_covered: That the j-invariant of a curve without an F-core is one of the four values (Proposition 2.1 itself, from [Sijs] Table 4 and [CanLift], Proposition 2.7), the notion of F-core, and the rest of IUT IV Corollary 2.2 (ii). The points of the lambda-line over the four values are printed neither on page 21 nor on IUT IV page 43; they are computed here from the printed values. Because the points checked here are not printed, this record is counted as a model test.
ambiguities: IUT IV does not list the four values; they are taken from Explicit estimates, Proposition 2.1. Proved here: legendreJ (1/9) = 2^2 73^3 3^-4 (legendreJ_one_ninth) and the six-point solution set of that value (legendreJ_eq_73_iff); so the point 1/9 of the triple 1 + 8 = 9 has this j-value. That this value is the j-invariant of a curve without an F-core (Explicit estimates, Proposition 2.1; [CanLift], Proposition 2.7) and that such points are excluded into Exc_d (IUT IV page 43) are statements of the papers, not proved here.

GENELL.Sec1.ArithmeticDivisor.content: Arithmetic divisors on a number field F: finite formal sums of valuations with integer coefficients at nonarchimedean and real coefficients at archimedean valuations, forming the group ADiv(F). The principal arithmetic divisor of f in F is ADiv(f) = sum over nonarchimedean v of ord_v(f) v minus sum over archimedean v of [F_v : R] log|f|_v v; these form the subgroup APrc(F). The degree map deg_F is defined on ADiv(F)/APrc(F), which is isomorphic to APic(Spec O_F) ([Szp], Proposition 1.1), by the weights log(q_v) at nonarchimedean and 1 at archimedean valuations, and the normalized degree (1/[F : Q]) deg_F is invariant under finite extension for arithmetic line bundles.
explicit_hypotheses: f a nonzero element of F
GENELL.Sec1.ArithmeticDivisor.conclusion: deg_F is a homomorphism on ADiv(F)/APrc(F), so it vanishes on principal arithmetic divisors; the normalized degree of an arithmetic line bundle is invariant under restriction to a finite extension.
obligations: The isomorphism ADiv(F)/APrc(F) = APic(Spec O_F) and arithmetic line bundles are not formalized; the principal divisor and the vanishing of the degree on it are (GENELL.Sec1.ArithmeticDivisor.frag.principal, GENELL.Sec1.ArithmeticDivisor.frag.degF_principal).

GENELL.Sec1.ArithmeticDivisor.frag.princ.content: The principal arithmetic divisor of x in K^x, as printed in [GenEll] page 4: coefficient ord_v(x) at a finite place v and -[K_v : R] log|x|_v at an archimedean place v ([K_v : R] = InfinitePlace.mult). ord_v(x) is minus WithZero.log of Mathlib's v-adic valuation.
GENELL.Sec1.ArithmeticDivisor.frag.princ.conclusion: Definition of degPbPrincipal (with degPbOrd and degPbPrincipalCoeff); its support is finite (degPbOrd_finite, degPbPrincipalCoeff_support_finite).
GENELL.Sec1.ArithmeticDivisor.frag.princ.covers: [GenEll] page 4, the display defining the principal arithmetic divisor ADiv(f). IUT IV Definition 1.9 (pages 21 and 22) recalls the notation of [GenEll] section 1 but prints no principal divisor; this display fixes the archimedean convention: the factor [F_v : R] is in the coefficient.
GENELL.Sec1.ArithmeticDivisor.frag.princ.not_covered: This is a definition: the kernel checks only that it is well typed. [GenEll] takes integer coefficients at finite places; here they are real numbers equal to integers. The subgroup APrc(F) and the isomorphism ADiv(F)/APrc(F) = APic(Spec O_F) are not formalized.

GENELL.Sec1.ArithmeticDivisor.frag.degF_.content: The degree deg_K (weight log q_v at finite places, 1 at archimedean places, as on [GenEll] page 4 and IUT IV page 21) of the principal arithmetic divisor of x in K^x is zero. Proof: log|x|_v = -ord_v(x) log q_v at finite places and Mathlib's product formula NumberField.prod_abs_eq_one.
GENELL.Sec1.ArithmeticDivisor.frag.degF_.covers: [GenEll] page 4: the degree map deg_F is printed with domain ADiv(F)/APrc(F) and the weights log(q_v) and 1, that is, as a map that is well defined on the quotient by the principal divisors; this record checks that deg_F vanishes on principal divisors. IUT IV pages 21 and 22 print the same weights but no principal divisor.
GENELL.Sec1.ArithmeticDivisor.frag.degF_.not_covered: The isomorphism with APic(Spec O_F) and the degree of arithmetic line bundles. The vanishing on principal divisors is not printed on the page as a sentence; it is an inference from the printed domain of deg_F, so this record is counted as a model test.
ambiguities: [GenEll] page 4 prints the vanishing only through the domain ADiv(F)/APrc(F) of deg_F, with a reference to [Szp] section 1.1.
